issues.t: Timing chain rattle or breakage
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine, especially on cold starts, misfires or rough idle. If the chain breaks, the engine dies suddenly while driving and won't restart.
issues.why: On early 2.2L engines the timing chain tensioner gets too little oil at idle and wears out, letting the chain slap and stretch. A broken chain can bend valves.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time. If you hear a rattle, have the chain, guides and tensioner replaced before the chain breaks and ruins the engine.

issues.t: Timing chain links can separate (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and will not restart.
issues.why: Some 2001 LS sedans built from November 2000 to February 2001 got timing chains whose links could separate. GM recalled about 20,500 cars (NHTSA 07V519).
issues.next: Have a Saturn/GM dealer check your VIN; the fix is a free timing chain.

issues.t: Ignition module failure causes rough idle and power loss (recall)
issues.sym: Rough idle, loss of power, hard starting and a flashing Service Engine Soon light. Later, a louder exhaust.
issues.why: The ignition control module on early 2.2L cars can fail. Driving on with misfires can damage the catalytic converter, oxygen sensor and exhaust resonator, and a failed resonator can lead to a fire. GM recalled about 240,000 cars (NHTSA 03V231).
issues.next: Stop driving with a flashing engine light. Have a dealer check your VIN; the recall replaces the module and may include new plugs and a computer update.

issues.t: Timing belt failure can wreck the engine
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The engine suddenly stops and won't start, or it slips a tooth and runs badly with a check engine light.
issues.why: The 3.0L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule. Owners report belts slipping or breaking and destroying the engine when it was skipped.
issues.next: If you don't have proof it was done, replace the timing belt, tensioner and idler pulleys now. Doing the water pump at the same time saves labor.

issues.t: Oil cooler or oil filter housing leak
issues.sym: Oil leaks near the oil filter, or worse, oil and coolant mixing into a light-brown sludge in the radiator or under the oil cap. The engine may overheat.
issues.why: The engine oil cooler, which sits in the valley of the V6, can crack and let oil and coolant mix. The plastic-and-metal oil filter housing can also crack or break its anti-rotation tab during oil changes.
issues.next: If you see milky oil or brown sludge in the coolant, stop driving and have it diagnosed. The cooler repair means removing the top of the engine, and the cooling system will need a thorough flush.

issues.t: Body control module failure
issues.sym: Gauges stop working, a constant chime, dash warning lights acting up, the odometer changing after a battery swap, or a car that starts but won't drive.
issues.why: The body control module, which runs many of the car's electrical features, fails on these cars. RepairPal lists it among the top L300 problems.
issues.next: Have all modules scanned for codes. A replacement module usually needs to be programmed to the car.

issues.t: Doors lock and unlock by themselves
issues.sym: The doors lock, then unlock on their own a few minutes later, or cycle while you drive.
issues.why: An electrical fault in the power lock system, such as a lock actuator, switch or the body control module. The cause is often hard to track down.
issues.next: Have a shop check the door lock actuators and switches first, since they are the cheapest parts to rule out.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold from a failed compressor
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, the compressor clutch doesn't engage, or there is a burning belt smell when the A/C runs.
issues.why: Owners report A/C compressor and clutch failures on both engines, often between 60,000 and 120,000 miles. Leaking hoses, condensers and evaporators also show up.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and the compressor clutch tested before recharging. Replace the receiver-drier along with the compressor.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic automatic shifting
issues.sym: Hard shifts, especially from first to second, a check engine or wrench light, or a transmission stuck in one gear until the car is restarted.
issues.why: Owners trace many cases to a failed pressure control solenoid or other valve body solenoids. Some transmissions need a full rebuild or replacement.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. Ask the shop about GM service bulletins for the solenoids before agreeing to a replacement transmission.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure leaves the car unable to start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or it loses power and sputters, sometimes with a fuel smell from a leaking pump seal.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out or leaks. Fuel pump complaints are among the most common for the 2003 L200.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested to confirm. If you smell raw fuel, get it fixed right away.

issues.t: No-start or stalling from a failed crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or stalls and won't restart until it cools down.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor tells the computer when to fire the plugs. When it fails, the engine gets no spark.
issues.next: Have the codes read; a scan tool can show whether the sensor is sending a signal while cranking.

issues.t: Check engine light with rough running
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle, misfires, backfiring, stalling or weak acceleration.
issues.why: Owners trace these to failed oxygen sensors, the EGR valve, the MAP sensor, ignition coils or vacuum leaks.
issues.next: Have the codes read and fix the specific fault. Don't ignore a flashing light; misfires can ruin the catalytic converters.

issues.t: Brake lights can fail from a warped tail lamp (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights or tail lights work only some of the time, or stop working after a blown fuse.
issues.why: If the brake lights stay on for a long time, the plastic tail lamp housing can warp, causing bad bulb contact or a short. GM recalled about 292,000 cars (NHTSA 05V245).
issues.next: Ask someone to check your brake lights. Have a dealer check your VIN; the fix adds reinforced sockets.

issues.t: Wagon rear seat belt anchor can pull loose (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal use.
issues.why: On some wagons the rear center seat belt anchor can separate from the floor in a crash. GM recalled about 20,700 wagons (NHTSA 05V158).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN; the fix adds a reinforcement plate.

issues.t: Turn signals can stop working from the hazard switch (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signals stop working.
issues.why: A faulty hazard warning switch can disable the turn signals. GM recalled these cars (NHTSA 99V199) to replace the switch.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for open recall work.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve could spill fuel in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: A fuel tank valve could be inoperative or stick open in a crash, letting fuel spill in a rollover. GM issued two recalls (NHTSA 99V197 and 99V345).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for both campaigns.

issues.t: Rear seat belt buckles may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal use.
issues.why: Some TRW buckle bases were not heat treated correctly and may not hold in a crash. GM recalled affected cars (NHTSA 00V228).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN; affected rear buckles are replaced free.

issues.t: Shifter can show Park when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter is in Park but the car rolls, or the gear shown doesn't match how the car behaves.
issues.why: On some 2001 LS sedans built in early October 2000, the shift cable clip was missing or loose, so the cable could slip out of its bracket. GM recalled them (NHTSA 00V344).
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have a dealer check your VIN.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working.
issues.why: Some 2003 cars built in mid-October 2002 got wiper motors with a manufacturing defect. GM recalled them (NHTSA 02V283).
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN.

issues.t: High beams come on with the left turn signal
issues.sym: Using the left turn signal switches the high beams on.
issues.why: No confirmed cause from owners; the steering column switch that controls both the signals and headlights, or its wiring, is the first thing to check.
issues.next: Have the multifunction switch and its connector checked.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or grinding
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed, sometimes changing in turns.
issues.why: Front and rear wheel bearings wear out on higher-mileage cars.
issues.next: Have the hubs checked for play and noise and replace the worn one.

issues.t: Power steering pump, hose or rack leaks
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks, a whining pump, rough or heavy steering in turns.
issues.why: Owners report leaking pumps, corroded return lines and worn steering racks.
issues.next: Keep the fluid topped off and find the leak; running the pump dry destroys it.

issues.t: Heater core or heater hose leak wets the floor
issues.sym: Wet passenger-side carpet, a sweet coolant smell inside, foggy windows, or coolant loss.
issues.why: Heater core O-rings, the heater core itself, and heater hose quick-connect fittings leak with age.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Fix it soon; coolant loss can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Check engine light from a loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative system leak code; the car runs normally.
issues.why: A loose, cracked or worn gas cap lets fuel vapor escape, which the emissions system reads as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks, or replace it. The light should clear after several days of driving.

issues.t: Bumper cover keeps coming loose
issues.sym: The bumper cover sags, rattles or falls off.
issues.why: Its clips and mounting points break.
issues.next: Have the clips and brackets replaced so it doesn't come off at speed.
